Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s records permit direct payments to every affected member, so automatic distribution is essential. We propose a $30 million class fund and a separately paid $7 million fee-and-expense request, subject to court approval. Any fee reduction would benefit the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that direct, automatic payments are appropriate. Brightline can offer a $25 million class fund and up to $5 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval. We would not seek clear sailing, and any fee reduction would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any court-reduced fees to the class. To narrow the remaining gap, we propose a $28 million class fund and $6 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with no clear-sailing provision.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $28 million class fund, $6 million in separately paid fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear sailing, any fee reduction benefiting the class, and automatic distribution.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial automatic-distribution fund reflecting the class’s litigation risk and potential recovery. Seek a fee subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. Avoid claims-made distribution and fee reversion.

The opening offer is within Brightline’s $40 million limit, but there is room to seek a lower total outlay. Automatic distribution and fee reductions benefiting the class support approval. I will counter without adding terms that could undermine approval.

The defense offer provides automatic payments and appropriate fee safeguards, but a $25 million fund is below the approximate $27.5 million trial-value estimate before accounting for certification and delay. A moderate counter preserves room to negotiate while seeking stronger class recovery and a defensible fee.

The $34 million total is below Brightline’s $40 million authorization. Automatic payments, no clear sailing, and fee reductions benefiting the class support court approval. Accepting now avoids further litigation expense and settlement risk.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). Counsel exchanged two rounds of proposals. Our initial proposal sought a $30 million class fund and $7 million in separately paid fees and expenses. Brightline countered with $25 million and $5 million. We then proposed a $28 million class fund and $6 million in separately paid fees and expenses, which Brightline accepted. Both sides agreed from the outset on automatic payments to identified class members, no clear-sailing provision, and payment of any court-reduced fees to the class rather than Brightline. Fees and class relief were discussed together throughout the negotiations; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. The $28 million fund represents approximately 44% of the $64 million in disputed charges and will be distributed automatically, without requiring claims. In assessing the settlement, we considered the risks of class certification and trial, including our assessment of an approximately 55% chance of prevailing at trial, as well as the two-to-three-year wait for a trial. The separately paid $6 million fee-and-expense amount remains subject to the Court’s approval. I believe the settlement warrants preliminary approval as fair, reasonable, and adequate for the class.
